Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro/demo this morning — helpful to see Redwood's runtime and the redaction/retention primitives you mentioned. As a quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can take this to legal/security: 

- We need confirmation that request and response bodies can be redacted at ingest with configurable rules (PII patterns + custom regex).
- Are headers and trace IDs removed from persisted request logs by default, or is that an opt-in config? We need to ensure trace IDs are not retained in logs for PCI-scoped flows.
- Retention windows: can we set per-customer log retention (e.g., 30/90/365 days) and auto-purge?
- Do you support deterministic masking (consistent pseudonyms) vs irreversible hashing for identifiers? Legal prefers irreversible hashing for some classes.

Could you send a short spec and any SOC2/audit artifacts we can share with our security team? Priya (cc) will lead the security review. Also copying Bob from our external security consultant for any technical clarifications.

Hi Alex / Priya / Bob,

Great to meet you all — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I attached a short redaction_spec_v1.xlsx that maps capabilities to configuration knobs. SOC2 evidence request attached as well. High-level: 

- Request/response redaction: supported both at ingest (recommended) and during export. You can apply built-in PII detectors (emails, SSNs, credit card numbers) and add custom regex rules. Rules run in the runtime before tokens are written to persistent logs.
- Headers & trace IDs: by default we redact Authorization and Cookie headers from persisted logging. Trace IDs are configurable — we can either strip them entirely or hash them before storage. For PCI-scoped traffic our recommendation is to strip trace IDs from persisted logs; we can enable default strip for any route labeled "pci".
- Retention windows: per-customer and per-route retention policies are supported (30/90/365/3650 days). Auto-purge runs daily and we provide an audit log of purge actions.
- Deterministic masking vs irreversible hashing: both supported. You can choose deterministic pseudonymization (useful for multi-request correlation) or irreversible hashes (sha256 with salt) when your policy requires non-reversible transformations.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical confirmation from our SEs on the hash salts and KMS workflows (sending to Vivek + Neha).
2) I'll share a concise one-page compliance summary for your security team and set up a 30-minute follow-up to walk through the redaction spec with Priya & Bob.
3) If acceptable, we can scope a short POC to demonstrate redaction for a small subset of production traffic (redacted copies only).

Attaching: redaction_spec_v1.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_request.pdf

Marissa / all — quick tech confirm below: 

- Runtime redaction: confirmed. Redaction rules execute during ingest at the tokenization boundary and we do not persist unredacted request/response bodies. There is a short in-memory buffer (sub-second) used for streaming; nothing persists to disk until after redaction.
- Trace IDs: default behavior is to strip Authorization/Cookie headers and to preserve trace IDs only in ephemeral traces. For persisted request logs we have 'trace_mode' with options: "strip", "hash", "retain". For PCI-tagged routes we'll set "strip" by default via a route policy.
- KMS + hashing: irreversible hashing uses HMAC-SHA256 with a KMS-managed salt. Salts are rotated every 90 days; rotation is handled by KMS and old salts are retained for decryption/verifiability only in metadata for 30 days before full deletion.
- Streaming redaction: we support streaming redaction at chunk boundary. That means we can redact in-flight tokens as chunks are finalized; deterministic pseudonyms are supported across chunks for the same session id when deterministic mode is enabled. A note: extremely low-latency single-token streaming may have a small window where the token is emitted before redaction completes — we document this and recommend chunked streaming for PCI scenarios.

If you want, I can prepare a short tech appendix for the POC that shows config snippets (route policy yaml, regex example, KMS key usage).

—Neha
